record.paper_title: Geodesic Nets: Some Examples and Open Problems
record.original_question: Let a geodesic net with exactly three unbalanced vertices A1, A2, A3 be drawn on a Riemannian plane, with geodesic edges and balanced vertices satisfying the zero-sum unit-tangent condition. Parsch proved that on any nonpositively curved Riemannian plane such a net has exactly one balanced vertex O at the Fermat point of A1, A2, A3 and exactly the three edges OA1, OA2, and OA3. Does the same rigidity conclusion remain true under the weaker assumption that the integral of the positive part of the curvature is sufficiently small?

evidence.quote: Theorem 3.1.2 ([Par18]). A geodesic net with 3 unbalanced vertices A1 , A2 , A3 in the Euclidean plane has exactly one balanced vertex O at the Fermat point of the three unbalanced vertices and three edges OAi . Moreover, this assertion is true for geodesic nets with 3 unbalanced vertices on any non-positively curved Riemannian R2 .

Yet it is not known if the assertion is still true if the integral of the positive part of the curvature is sufficiently small. (The example for positive curvature constructed in [Par18] requires total curvature at least π.)

artifact.self_contained_problem: Let (R^2, g) be a smooth complete Riemannian metric on the plane with Gaussian curvature K. A geodesic net in (R^2, g) is a finite graph whose vertices are points of R^2 and whose edges are geodesic segments joining them; each vertex v is classified as balanced if the sum of the unit tangent vectors at v of the edges incident to v is zero, and otherwise unbalanced. It is known that if K ≤ 0 everywhere, then any geodesic net having exactly three unbalanced vertices A_1, A_2, A_3 must consist of exactly one balanced vertex O, located at the Fermat point of A_1, A_2, A_3, together with the three edges OA_1, OA_2, OA_3. Question: does there exist a constant ε > 0 such that the same rigidity conclusion (exactly one balanced vertex O, the Fermat point of {A_1, A_2, A_3}, with the three edges OA_1, OA_2, OA_3 and no others) holds for every smooth complete Riemannian metric g on R^2 satisfying ∫_{R^2} max(K, 0) dA_g < ε, for every geodesic net in (R^2, g) with exactly three unbalanced vertices?
artifact.status_search_result: A search did not produce a resolution. The problem is stated as not known, with an existing positive-curvature counterexample requiring total positive curvature at least π, but no result establishing rigidity (or producing a counterexample) under a small positive-curvature integral assumption was found.

status_evidence.title: Geodesic Nets: Some Examples and Open Problems
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses rigidity of geodesic nets with three unbalanced vertices and notes the case of small positive curvature integral as not known.
status_evidence.claim: The question of whether the rigidity remains under small total positive curvature is recorded as an open problem.
